assertions.description: The GamepadButton interface — the exact interface the spec PR extends with `partial interface GamepadButton` — is exposed.
The documented feature-detection passes: 'type' in GamepadButton.prototype (fails honestly wherever the GamepadButtonTypes flag is off or the implementation has not landed).
GamepadButton.prototype.type is a readonly accessor per `readonly attribute GamepadButtonType type` — a getter with no setter.

Every button of every currently connected gamepad reports a type inside the exact three-value enum {"non-standard","standard","trackpad"}; fails when the attribute is missing, and passes vacuously (no counter-example) when supported but no pad is connected.
assertions.test: (()=>{if(typeof GamepadButton==='undefined'||!('type' in GamepadButton.prototype)||typeof navigator.getGamepads!=='function')return false;const vocab=['non-standard','standard','trackpad'];for(const p of navigator.getGamepads()){if(!p)continue;for(const b of p.buttons){if(!vocab.includes(b.type))return false;}}return true;})()

assertions.description: On a controller with an integrated touchpad (DualShock 4 / DualSense), the touchpad click button reports type "trackpad" — the proposal's canonical use case.
assertions.test: Requires a physical controller with a touchpad, connected and woken with a button press, in a browser with GamepadButtonTypes enabled; verify via the Live Button Inspector that the touchpad click's type pill reads "trackpad".

assertions.description: Backward compatibility: gamepad button state objects are still GamepadButton platform instances with pressed/touched/value, so existing content keeps working whether or not `type` is present (executes cleanly on any browser with the base Gamepad API).
assertions.test: (()=>{if(typeof GamepadButton==='undefined')return false;const proto=GamepadButton.prototype;return ('pressed' in proto)&&('touched' in proto)&&('value' in proto);})()
